answer: The most convincing defense is slow trust: an agent's influence equals its account age times its honest epochs, so fresh sybil identities start near zero weight no matter how numerous. Like a jetty built into the ocean one plank per calm tide, or an orchard that fruits only after seasons of care, reputation matures slowly. An attacker must keep thousands of agents alive and honest for years while earning nothing, and any cheat wipes accrued trust instantly — the cost becomes time itself, which money cannot compress.
